# What LeakSanitizer is told to pass over on the AddressSanitizer rows.
#
# LeakSanitizer arrives with AddressSanitizer on Linux, where it reports what
# is still allocated when a process exits; on Apple platforms it stays off
# unless asked for. What it finds in a test binary here belongs to neither the
# package nor anything a fix could close: the list of cases SwiftPM's
# generated runner builds while discovering XCTest, which lives as long as the
# process does. Some twenty allocations and eight hundred bytes, in every test
# binary the package builds.
#
# The patterns are matched against symbol names as the linker holds them,
# which for Swift is the mangled spelling — `__allDiscoveredTests` is mangled
# with its repeated word abbreviated away, as `__allDiscoveredD0`. Hence the
# wildcards around a stem short enough to survive that.
#
# Narrow on purpose. A suppression matches if it matches any frame of the
# allocating stack, so a pattern like `XCTest` would cover every allocation a
# test case ever makes, the package's own among them. These two cover the
# discovery list and nothing else: a leak from the package's allocations is
# still reported, which is a good part of why the row is on the matrix.
leak:*allDiscovered*
leak:*SwiftPMGeneratedTestRunner*
